To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the liquid crystalline stationary phase is a unique tool in the separation of organic mixtures, especially in the case of isomeric mixtures, which are difficult to separate using traditional partition gas chromatography.

the liquid crystal stationary phases (LC-SPs) have high selectivity, and they can be used for the separation of isomeric and homologous compounds, which are not possible by the use of conventional gas chromatography (GC) stationary phases.
the liquid crystals as stationary phases in chromatography can be used to identify analyte mixtures with high selectivity.
